source_ref: Luna-Cortes G, Lopez-Bonilla LM, Lopez-Bonilla JM (2019) PLoS ONE 14(6):e0217758, doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0217758 (CC BY 4.0); Table 1 'Items of the scales' (Perceived Social Value [PSV] block, 3 bullets), image only, https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0217758.t001; Table 2 'Reliability and convergent validity' (PSV1/PSV2 loadings, alpha 0.822), https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0217758.t002; S1 File XLSX headers 'Social-Val1'..'Social-Val3', doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0217758.s001; processing script data/lunacortes_2019_vsn_scales.py
note: Item wording transcribed from the PLOS article's Table 1 'Items of the scales', which PLOS publishes only as an IMAGE (the .t001 HTML endpoint carries no item text) -- read from the PNG at journals.plos.org/plosone/article/figure/image?size=large&id=10.1371/journal.pone.0217758.t001 (fetched 2026-09-08, cached under itemtext/.cache/lunacortes_2019_social_value/), so the transcription is a fallible image read and worth a human spot-check. The three Perceived Social Value [PSV] bullets carry no per-item numbering, so bullet order was taken to be the PSV1/PSV2/PSV3 numbering Table 2 uses; hence mapping_basis=paper_order, not paper_explicit. CODE DERIVATION (exempt-eligible, checked anyway): data/lunacortes_2019_vsn_scales.py renames the S1 File XLSX headers 'Social-Val1'..'Social-Val3' by lowercasing and mapping '-'->'_' and melts BY NAME, so the IRW code IS the source column name with no positional step -- confirmed cell-for-cell, all three live columns identical to their namesake source columns over 444 respondents (verify_lunacortes_2019_social_value.R, link A). MAPPING EVIDENCE (Step 5b, PARTIAL): section 3.4 states that 'the third item on the Perceived Social Value Scale (PSV3) presented factor loadings lower than the rest of the items' and was removed on the Lagrange test, which is why Table 2 lists only PSV1 (0.83) and PSV2 (0.84) while the data has three columns. That makes Table 2's Cronbach's alpha of 0.822 a two-item fingerprint: alpha{social_val1,social_val2}=0.8219 against 0.3447 and 0.4576 for the other two pairs (and 0.6835 for all three), so social_val3 is the dropped PSV3. It is also the weakest indicator on its own (corrected item-total r=0.2792 vs 0.5912 and 0.6643) and the easiest to endorse (mean 5.383, SD 1.316, vs 4.556/1.590 and 4.698/1.597), which matches bullet 3 'makes a good impression on other people' being the semantic odd one out -- about others' impression rather than the respondent's own social standing. NOT ESTABLISHED: social_val1 vs social_val2, whose published loadings 0.83 and 0.84 carry an IDENTICAL robust t of 24.100; that pairing rests on bullet order alone. ADMINISTERED LANGUAGE: the survey was interviewed in Spanish (section 3.2 'These interviews were taken in Spanish'; section 3.3 documents a four-step forward translation of the scales from English into Spanish by the lead author), but no Spanish wording is published anywhere in the record -- the only supplement is S1 File, the response XLSX, whose 22 headers are the bare codes 'Number','SATIS 1'..,'Social-Val1'..'Social-Val3',.. with no label row and no Spanish text, and the article prints English only. So the 2026-09-01 fallback applies: English in the base fields, language=Spanish, empty _translated columns, text_source=translated_substitute, translation_source=study_supplied (the English is the authors' own source wording as printed in their Table 1). Note section 3.3 also records that the pre-test changed some Spanish verbs to easier synonyms, so the administered Spanish is not a strict rendering of this English even in principle. SCALE ANCHORS: only the two endpoints are labelled in the source ('a Likert scale of seven points (from 1-totally disagree, to 7-totally agree)', section 3.2); resp 2-6 were left with blank option_text rather than padded with their own numbers. No instructions text is printed anywhere in the article, so instructions is blank. STEP 3b: clean -- the live table is 3 items on resp 1-7 with the Table 1 [PSV] block's item count, and the dictionary Description ('3-item perceived social value scale (1-7 Likert)') matches; it is not one of the five other scales in the same S1 File (SATIS 3, Self-Cong 4, ISNCC 4, IC 4, ISNBI 3). RIGHTS: wording taken from a CC BY 4.0 PLOS ONE article. The underlying PERVAL social-value scale (Sweeney and Soutar 2001, Journal of Retailing) has no quotable licence fee or no-redistribution clause that could be found, so silence-is-permission applies and neither 2026-09-04 trigger fires. COVERAGE: all 3 items x all 7 resp levels shipped; per-item n is 444/444/444 with all seven levels used by every item (irw_table_sets, server-side). SIBLINGS: lunacortes_2019_satisfaction was shipped in batch_089 from the same Table 1 image; lunacortes_2019_self_congruity, lunacortes_2019_interperson_conn, lunacortes_2019_isnbi and lunacortes_2019_isncc remain queued and nothing was written for them here.
public_note: Item wording for this table comes from the source article's Table 1, which PLOS publishes only as an image, and its three bullets are unnumbered -- the assignment of wording to social_val1/social_val2/social_val3 follows bullet order. social_val3 is pinned independently: the paper dropped its third PSV item from the CFA, and the published two-item Cronbach's alpha of 0.822 is reproduced only by the pair social_val1+social_val2 (0.8219, against 0.34 and 0.46 for the other pairs), while social_val3 is also the weakest indicator in the data (item-total 0.28 vs 0.59 and 0.66). The social_val1 vs social_val2 ordering is not pinned, since the paper's loadings for those two (0.83, 0.84) share an identical robust t. The instrument was administered in Spanish; the shipped text is the English the authors translated from, as the Spanish wording is not published

source_ref: Luo M, Zhang X, Peng F, Zhao J, Deng H (2021) Predictors of acculturation attitude of international students in China. PLOS ONE 16(11):e0260616, doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0260616 (CC BY 4.0); S3 File dataset doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0260616.s003 (.sav, 229 rows x 65 columns, cached under itemtext/.cache/luo_2021_conational_ties/s003.sav) -- the four co-national columns are at 1-based positions 32-35 and carry their own item wording in the COLUMN NAME; processing script data/luo_2021_acculturation.py; instrument Winefield HR, Winefield AH, Tiggemann M (1992) Social support and psychological well-being in young adults: the multi-dimensional support scale. J Pers Assess 58(1):198-210; truncated item tails completed from the MDSS wording printed verbatim in Wei X (2025) Front Psychol 16:1607241, doi:10.3389/fpsyg.2025.1607241, PMC12314320 (CC BY), fetched 2026-09-08
note: TEXT SOURCE AND THE ONE REAL CAVEAT: the S3 File .sav carries no variable labels for these items (only the block header 'Co-national ties' on the first column) -- the item wording is the COLUMN NAME itself, which SPSS stores space-stripped and capped at 64 characters. All four co-national names are exactly 64 characters, i.e. all four are truncated mid-word: 'Conationalties1.Howoftendidyourconationalfriendsreallylistentoyo', '@2.Howoftendidyourconationalfriendstrytotakeyourmindoffyourprobl', '@3.Howoftendidyourconationalfriendshelpyouinpracticalwayslikedoi', '@4.Howoftendidyourconationalfriendsansweryouquestionsorgiveyouad'. So 48-61 characters of each shipped sentence are the study's own words and the TAIL of each is not. The tails were completed from the MDSS question wording printed verbatim in Wei X (2025) Front Psychol 16:1607241 (PMC12314320), which reproduces the scale as five questions: '(1) How often did your host international friends really listen to you when you talked about your concerns or problems? (2) How often did you feel that they were really trying to understand your problems? (3) How often did they try to take your mind off your problems by telling jokes or chattering about other things? (4) How often did they help you in practical ways, like doing things for you or lending you money? (5) How often did they answer your questions or give you advice about how to solve your problems?' Luo's four items are that list minus (2), and each truncated prefix identifies exactly one of the five without ambiguity. The completions are independently corroborated INSIDE the same .sav: the parallel host-friends (positions 36-39) and international-friends (40-43) blocks are the same four questions with a longer/shorter group name, so they truncate at different points and extend the prefixes further -- 'reallylistentoyouwhen', 'takeyourmindoffyourproblemsbyt', 'likedoingthin', 'giveyouadviceab' -- all consistent with the Wei rendering. DEVIATIONS, all deliberate: (a) word spacing and punctuation are unrecoverable from an SPSS name and were restored (the comma in 'practical ways, like doing things' comes from Wei, not from the source); (b) the group name is written 'co-national friends' following the paper's own prose ('Co-national friends (same nationality friends)') -- the .sav name reads 'conationalfriends' because SPSS strips hyphens as well as spaces, so the hyphen is a reconstruction; (c) item_04 keeps the study's own typo 'answer you questions' -- the de-spaced name is 'answeryouquestions', which cannot be 'answer your questions' (that would de-space to 'answeryourquestions'), so the missing 'r' is the study's and was not silently corrected. MAPPING (paper_explicit / positional derivation, VERIFIED): data/luo_2021_acculturation.py assigns item_01..item_04 POSITIONALLY (CONATIONAL_IDX = range(31,35), then f'item_{i+1:02d}'), so the code keeps no trace of the source name and the positional header diff was run rather than assumed. It is decisive here: each item's live 4-cell response distribution equals the .sav column at the claimed position cell for cell -- item_01 25/57/75/72, item_02 23/67/76/63, item_03 24/71/61/73, item_04 21/69/63/76, 16/16 cells, and the four distributions are pairwise distinct so exactly 1 of the 24 possible code permutations fits (verify_luo_2021_conational_ties.R sections A and B). Note the MEANS do not do this: item_01 and item_04 both average 2.847162, which is why the check compares frequency cells. Section C then confirms each shipped sentence begins with that column's own 48-61 characters. OPTIONS: the paper states 'Each source of social support is measured with 4 items on a 4-point Likert scale (1 = never, 4 = always)' and nothing anywhere labels points 2 and 3, so option_text is shipped for resp 1 and 4 only and left BLANK for 2 and 3 rather than padded with their own numbers. The .sav carries no value labels at all (variable_value_labels is empty for every one of the 65 columns). LANGUAGE: administered in English -- Yangtze University international students, the questionnaire columns are English, and the study measures self-rated English and Chinese proficiency as covariates; the only non-ASCII strings in the whole file are the two trailing SPSS QCL_1/QCL_2 cluster-diagnostic columns, which the processing script drops. So no language / _translated columns are emitted. INSTRUCTIONS: none published. Neither the paper nor the .sav carries a stem, a recall window, or any framing text for this block, so instructions and section_prompt are blank rather than invented; the MDSS's own 'in the last month' window (as Wei reports it) was NOT shipped because Luo never states it. STEP 3b: clean -- 4 items on resp 1-4 is the co-national block and not one of the four other instruments in the same file (ECR-SF 12 items 1-7, host ties 4 items, international ties 4 items, Acculturation Index 10 items 1-5); the two sibling ties blocks are separate IRW tables, and the column-position fingerprint above rules out a mix-up with them. RIGHTS: neither 2026-09-04 trigger fires -- no fee and no no-redistribution clause could be quoted for the MDSS, and under 'silence is permission' it was extracted normally; the deposit is PLOS CC BY 4.0 and the third-party rendering used for the tails is Frontiers CC BY. QUOTA: irw_fetch() was used once on this table for the mapping check (916 rows, 3 substantive columns) rather than for the Step 5 gate, which ran with --table-sets. SIBLINGS luo_2021_ecr and lunacortes_2019_social_value are owned by other agents in this round; nothing was written for either. RETRY TEST: not applicable, the table passed -- no access failure was hit (article, S3 File .sav and the Wei article all fetched first time).
public_note: The four SPSS column names that carry this instrument's wording are capped at 64 characters and all four are cut off mid-word, so only the first 48-61 characters of each shipped question are the study's own text; the remainder of each sentence, and all punctuation and word spacing, were completed from the same four Multi-Dimensional Support Scale questions as printed in Wei (2025, Front Psychol 16:1607241). Which of the four MDSS questions each item code is remains exact -- each item's live response distribution matches its source column cell for cell (25/57/75/72, 23/67/76/63, 24/71/61/73, 21/69/63/76), and only 1 of the 24 possible orderings fits. Scale points 2 and 3 carry no option text because the study labels only 1 = never and 4 = always

source_ref: Luo M, Zhang X, Peng F, Zhao J, Deng H (2021) Predictors of acculturation attitude of international students in China. PLOS ONE 16(11):e0260616, doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0260616 (CC BY 4.0); item wording from the study's own S3 File SPSS deposit doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0260616.s003, whose variable NAMES at columns 9,10,11,12,13,14,16,17,19,21,23,25 carry the 12 ECR-S item sentences (whitespace-stripped, e.g. 'AttachmentScale1.IwanttogetclosetomypartnerbutIkeeppullingback'); item 3's tail and the response anchors from the paper body; instrument Wei M, Russell DW, Mallinckrodt B, Vogel DL (2007) The Experiences in Close Relationship Scale (ECR)-Short Form. J Pers Assess 88(2):187-204; processing script data/luo_2021_acculturation.py
note: CLEAN PASS WITH A TRANSCRIPTION CAVEAT. TEXT: the words come from the study's own SPSS variable NAMES in S3 File -- SPSS names cannot contain spaces or commas, so every header is a run-together string ('@5.Itrytoavoidgettingtooclosetomypartner'). Word boundaries and punctuation were therefore RESTORED by this project, not transcribed; the curly apostrophes in items 3 and 11 are the source's own (U+2019). The leading item numbering ('@5.', 'AttachmentScale1.') was stripped. One header is TRUNCATED at SPSS's 64-character variable-name limit: column 11 ends '...asIcareabou', and its tail was completed from the paper's own verbatim quote of that item, 'I worry that romantic partners won't care about me as much as I care about them'. The restored sentences are word-for-word identical to the published ECR-S (Wei et al. 2007) with one difference, item 11, where the study writes 'my partners' and the published form writes 'my partner(s)'; the study's form is what ships. MAPPING (data_labels, but NOT exempt): data/luo_2021_acculturation.py assigns codes POSITIONALLY (ECR_IDX = [9,10,11,12,13,14,16,17,19,21,23,25], renamed f'item_{i+1:02d}'), so the positional header diff was run rather than asserted -- see verify_luo_2021_ecr.R, which reproduces all 12 x 7 = 84 per-item response-frequency cells from the .sav columns at exactly those indices against the live table, with all 12 source frequency vectors mutually distinct. OPTIONS: the paper states 'a seven-point scale ranging from 1 (strongly disagree) to 7 (strongly agree)'. Only the two endpoints are labelled anywhere, so resp 2-6 ship blank option_text rather than padded with their own numbers. DIRECTION / REVERSE CODING: the .sav also holds the authors' own reverse-scored duplicates @6R, @8R, @9R, @10R, @11R and @12R; the processing script drops all six and keeps the unreversed columns, so the IRW table stores RAW responses and the shipped anchors are not inverted. Corroborated by content: item_06 ('I usually discuss my problems and concerns with my partner') has the table's highest mean at 4.83 while item_02 ('I am nervous when partners get too close to me') has one of the lowest at 2.84 -- the expected direction if 7 = strongly agree. STEP 3b: clean. The paper's Methods name 'Meifen Wei and Daniel W. Russell's ECR Scale-Short Form ... 12 items ... two dimensions ... seven-point scale', matching the live 12 items on resp 1-7 exactly; the other instruments in the same file are 4-item/5-point social-tie batteries and a 10-item 5-point acculturation index, neither of which fits. RIGHTS: neither 2026-09-04 trigger fires. The ECR family is distributed without fee or restriction (R. Chris Fraley's measures pages supply ECR/ECR-R item content and scoring freely for research and clinical use), no fee licence or no-redistribution clause could be found or quoted for the ECR-S, and in any case the wording shipped here is lifted from the study's own CC BY 4.0 PLOS deposit rather than from a rights-holder edition. Silence is permission. LANGUAGE: administered in English (English-medium survey of international students in China; the paper reports Chinese and English proficiency as separate covariates), so no _translated columns. SIBLING: luo_2021_conational_ties, luo_2021_host_ties, luo_2021_intl_ties and luo_2021_acculturation_index come from the same S3 File; nothing was written for any of them.
